inline_comments.comment: The diff renames the second test case to 'should generate preview.tsx' and changes the expectation for the Angular-specific test from `.ts` to `.tsx`. However, the implementation in `configure.ts` only applies the `.tsx`/`.jsx` extension for JSX-based renderers (React, Preact, Solid, React Native). Angular does not use JSX, so this test expectation is incorrect — it should remain `.ts`. The test name 'should generate preview.tsx' is also too generic and would mislead readers into thinking all renderers get `.tsx`. The correct expectation for the Angular test case is `.storybook/preview.ts`.

After this PR, there are effectively two distinct behaviors (JSX extension for React-like renderers, plain extension otherwise), but the existing tests only cover one path each. A test explicitly asserting that non-React renderers like Angular or Vue continue to produce `.ts`/`.js` — not `.tsx`/`.jsx` — would guard against future regressions where the renderer check is accidentally removed.

This snippet documents an addon's own internal preview source file at `example-addon/src/preview.js`, not the user's `.storybook/preview.js`. Renaming the addon source file to `example-addon/src/preview.jsx` is out of scope for this PR and may mislead addon authors into thinking their addon's preview entry point must use a JSX extension. Only `.storybook/preview.*` (the project config file) is the target of this change.

The filename was `".storybook/preview.js|jsx"` (indicating either `.js` or `.jsx`), but the replacement is `".storybook/preview.jsx|jsx"`, which now has a redundant `|jsx` suffix — `preview.jsx|jsx` is nonsensical. It should simply be `".storybook/preview.jsx"`. The same issue appears in the TSX variant around line 51 (`preview.tsx|tsx`), and again around lines 205 and 229 in the CSF Next blocks. Compare the handling in `mock-context-container-global.md`, where the equivalent change is correctly simplified to just `.storybook/preview.jsx` / `.storybook/preview.tsx` with no trailing `|jsx` or `|tsx`.

The Svelte renderer's preview file is now shown as `.storybook/preview.tsx`. Svelte components live in `.svelte` files; the preview configuration file for Svelte does not contain JSX and has no reason to use the `.tsx` extension. The Storybook CLI (with the renderer-aware `isJsx` logic) would actually generate `.storybook/preview.ts` for Svelte projects, making this documentation snippet incorrect. The same applies to the web-components block below it — Lit uses HTML template literals, not JSX.

The Svelte preview snippet now uses `.storybook/preview.tsx`. This is inconsistent with what Storybook's CLI would actually generate for a Svelte project (`.preview.ts`), since Svelte is not a JSX renderer. Svelte decorators use `.svelte` component files imported into the preview, not JSX — a `.tsx` filename suggests JSX support that isn't needed or expected.

Similarly to line 1, the TypeScript variant renames `example-addon/src/preview.ts` to `example-addon/src/preview.tsx`. This is an addon source file, not a `.storybook/preview.ts` user config file. Addon preview entry points don't need to be `.tsx` — they typically export `ProjectAnnotations` without any JSX. This change may mislead addon authors.

The title attribute is updated to `".storybook/preview.jsx|tsx"`. This mixes JS and TS extensions in a single title string in a way that is confusing — `|` here implies either/or but `.jsx` is the JS variant and `.tsx` is the TS variant, which aren't interchangeable. The correct form matching the existing convention used elsewhere in the docs would be `".storybook/preview.jsx|tsx"` only if you intend to display both JS and TS options together; more clearly, the two variants should use `".storybook/preview.jsx"` and `".storybook/preview.tsx"` in their respective code blocks. Contrast with the `main.js|ts` pattern used in the same section which has separate blocks.

The `previewFilePath` is hardcoded to `preview.tsx` for the `react-vite-default-ts` sandbox, which is correct since React is a JSX renderer. However, if there are other sandboxes that exercise non-React renderers (Angular, Vue, Svelte) and their e2e tests similarly reference a preview file path, those would need to remain `.ts` — not `.tsx`. Consider adding a comment or assertion to make the React-specific reason explicit, so future contributors don't copy this pattern for non-React sandboxes.

general_comments.comment: There is a significant mismatch between the documentation changes and the actual code behavior. The diff updates virtually all renderer-specific documentation snippets — including Angular, Vue, Svelte, and Web Components — to show `.storybook/preview.tsx` / `.storybook/preview.jsx`. However, the actual `configure.ts` implementation uses a renderer-aware `isJsx` flag that only applies the `.tsx`/`.jsx` extension for React, Preact, Solid, and React Native. Angular, Vue, Svelte, and Web Components projects will still have `.storybook/preview.ts` / `.storybook/preview.js` generated by the CLI. This means the documentation will actively mislead users of non-JSX frameworks: they will see `.storybook/preview.tsx` in every doc snippet but find a `.storybook/preview.ts` file on disk. All renderer-specific snippets for Angular, Vue, Svelte, and Web Components should continue to use `.ts`/`.js` extensions in their `filename=` attributes.

Several documentation pages now reference `preview.jsx|tsx` (mixing JS and TS extensions in a single title string) in headings and inline code like `docs/api/csf/csf-next.mdx` and `docs/api/parameters.mdx`. This particular notation was not consistently used before this PR: the codebase historically used either `preview.js|ts` (the plain variants) or separate language-specific snippets. If the intent is to show both variants, the conventional form `preview.jsx|tsx` should be consistently applied everywhere it appears — and avoided in contexts where only one language (TS or JS) applies.

The AGENTS.md update and all prose documentation changes consistently rename `preview.ts` → `preview.tsx` and `preview.js` → `preview.jsx` regardless of renderer context. This is fine for the general/project-level documentation where renderer-neutral phrasing applies. However, framework-specific documentation pages (Angular, Vue, Svelte, Web Components) should preserve `.ts`/`.js` to match the files those users actually have on disk. The breadth of this change — hundreds of snippet files updated globally — makes it easy to introduce silent inaccuracies in renderer-specific sections, as seen with the Svelte and Web Components blocks.
